sentences.text: Dwardius is an extinct genus of sharks belonging to the class Chondrichthyes and the family Cardabiodontidae.
The genus was described by Mikael Siverson in 1999, elevating the species Cretalamna woodwardi, originally described by J. Hermann in 1977.
A second species, D. siversoni, was described by V.I. Zhelezko in 2000 from fossils found in the middle Albian of northeastern France.
In 2011, Underwood, Goswami, Prasad, Verma, and Flynn described D. sudindicus from the Cretaceous Karai Formation in India.
Dwardius is classified within the parent group Cardabiodontidae.
These sharks lived from the Aptian to the Santonian stages, between 121.4 and 83.6 million years ago.
Their range included regions that are now Australia, England, France, and India.
